# PR #4172: Patch: the fuzz forges the Trade and Marketplace actions its legal list never offered

Closes #4143

## What changed

The fuzz's I8 check (`unlisted_accepted` in `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`) now also forges the economic actions. A `reduce` that accepts one the legal list doesn't offer is reported as `I8 unlisted … accepted`, in the same message shape as the other I8 findings.

- **Forges:**
  - A `trade` and a `marketSell` for every card in the seat's hand, whether or not it is Tradable or sells. An accepted forge of an ineligible card is the bug class this check exists for.
  - A `marketBuy` for every offer index the Marketplace holds, including the other seat's lots and out-of-range indices.
- **Cost and placement:**
  - `accepts` skips any body the list already holds, so listed deals cost no extra `reduce`.
  - The block sits next to the switch, attack and activation forges and is not behind the `pending` / `mulligan` / `result` guard. A deal accepted while a prompt is open, or after the game is over, is therefore caught.
- **Citations:** the messages cite §10.2, R1838000 (trade), R1853003 and R2250002 (buy), and R1853003 and R1861000 (sale).
- **Docs:** the I8 prose names the new kinds in the oracle header and the doc comments in `invariants.rs`, in the `fuzz.rs` module doc, and in the `fuzz` row of `crates/tools/README.md`.
- **Stride:** `I8_GATE_STRIDE` stays 100. Its comment now holds the measured cost: `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` took 50 s before and 51 s after, on 4 cores, measured on the same machine back to back. Both runs had 0 invariant violations, so the new forges found nothing on seeds 1–200.

# #4143: Patch: the fuzz forges the Trade and Marketplace actions its legal list never offered
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A player at the table sees which moves are offered and can only pick those. Today the automated game-player checks that promise for attacks, moves, card plays and card powers, but not for trading in a card or buying and selling at the shop. Once built, a game where the rules engine quietly accepts a trade or a shop deal that was never offered fails the test run with a message naming the move, before it can reach real players. For example, using a trade a second time in one turn, or buying a shop card without enough coins, would be caught even though no button offered it.

## Why

The server applies a move without asking what the menus offered (see the I8 header in the oracle: "as the server reduces without `legal_actions`"). Trade is limited (once a turn, `TRADES_PER_TURN`, R1838000) and shop deals check coins, tickets, stock and turn phase (R1853003, R2250002). The oracle function `unlisted_accepted` in `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` forges only `SwitchPosition`, `Attack`, `activate`/`activatePower` and `play` from the board and hand; a search for `trade`, `marketBuy` or `marketSell` in that file finds only report payload readers, no forged bodies. The converse check I14 (every listed action is accepted) does not cover this direction, and the gate docs in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` describe I8 as covering only "play, attack, switch or activation". So an unlisted economic action that `reduce` accepts is currently silent.

## Proposal

Extend `unlisted_accepted` to forge the economic bodies: a `trade` for each Tradable hand card when the listing holds no trade of it (including the already-traded-this-turn case), a `marketBuy` for each shop offer index (including out-of-stock, short-of-coins and wrong-phase cases), and a `marketSell` for an eligible and an ineligible hand card. Reuse the existing `accepts`/`accepts_as` helpers on the cloned probe state with `PROBE_NONCE`, and report with the same `I8 unlisted ... accepted` message shape citing SPEC §10.2 and the Trade/Marketplace rules. Update the I8 paragraph in the oracle header and the gate list in `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` to name the new forged kinds. No rules change and no new ruling: this holds existing refusals, it does not decide one.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs`: `unlisted_accepted`, the I8 header docs, `I8_GATE_STRIDE` comment if the cost moves
- `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`: gate/I8 prose ("play, attack, switch or activation" line)
- SPEC sections read, not changed: §10.2 (actions), §10.8 (listings), §6.3 Trade and Marketplace, R1838000, R1838001, R1853003, R2250002

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A unit test crafts a state where no `trade` is listed (e.g. after one trade) and shows an accepted forged `trade` is reported as `I8 unlisted`.
- [ ] A unit test crafts a shop state short of coins (or with empty stock) and shows an accepted forged `marketBuy` is reported as `I8 unlisted`.
- [ ] A forged `marketSell` of a card with no sale quote that `reduce` accepts is likewise reported.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit` and the tools regression corpus stay green, with the stride cost noted (precedent: I8 stride 100 kept 103s near 104s).

## Size and risks

Medium: two files plus tests, test-only, no catalog or balance change. Risk is fuzz time if every offer is forged on every sampled state; mitigate by forging one body per card/offer and keeping the existing stride, measuring before/after as the stride comments do. Rejected alternative: re-checking the listing on the server instead of in fuzz; rejected because the server deliberately reduces without the listing, so the oracle must stay in the fuzz monitor.
